title: Building an Agentic Phone Answering System: 5 Design Principles
desc:
Many businesses miss more calls than they think: after hours, at lunch, or when everyone is busy with a customer. Every missed call is a customer someone else booked. An agentic phone answering system can pick up every call, day or night, answer common questions, take messages and book appointments. Here are five design principles for getting one right.

1. Write the job description first: who calls, what they want, and what a good outcome looks like.
2. Set the rules: what it can say, what it never says, and what it does when it doesn't know.
3. Keep it human: short answers, a natural voice, one question at a time.
4. Test it like a customer, then fix what breaks.
5. Know where it stops, and hand the call to a person.

It doesn't replace good people. It covers the calls they can't get to.

title: Nine AI Agents That Check Every Maintenance Work Order Before It Hits the Schedule
desc:
An agentic planning system for maintenance puts nine AI agents between planning and scheduling, each with one job: planning accuracy, background review of every work order, exception management, best planner practices, task lists, regulatory items and deferrals, reporting, human verification, and a planning quality hub where planners, leads and leadership act.

Why it matters: when a work order is missing a step, the right craft, the parts or the hours, nobody finds out until the crew is standing at the job.

Five design principles for building one:
1. Fix the plan, not the schedule.
2. Define what a complete work order looks like.
3. Let the AI check every work order, every time.
4. Split the fixes by risk.
5. Draw hard lines the AI can't cross. Safety and regulatory items always go to a person.

Better plans going in means a better schedule coming out.
